title: C482/1512/2023 of GUDDU LAL Vs STATE OF UTTARAKHAND

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
C482 No.1512 of 2023
With
IA/1/2023(Compounding Application)
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.
Mr. Saurav Adhikari, learned counsel for
the applicant.
Mr. A.K. Sah, learned Deputy Advocate
General for the State.
 Mr. B.S. Bhandari, learned counsel for
respondent no.2.
The instant C482 Application has been
preferred for the purpose of composition of
offence under Section 354 of the IPC for which
the applicant has been convicted by the
judgment dated 22.06.2022 of Criminal Case
No.1221 of 2019, "State Vs. Guddu Lal"
whereby though he has been acquitted for the
offence under Section 452 of the IPC; but for
the offence under Section 354 of the IPC, he
has been convicted and directed to undergo a
sentence of one year's simple imprisonment and
a fine of Rs.500/- has been imposed upon him.
The applicant/ convict, being aggrieved
against the said judgment of conviction, has
preferred an appeal, being Criminal Appeal
No.52 of 2022, "Guddu Lal Vs. State" and the
same is pending consideration before the Court
of Second Additional District and Sessions

Judge, Haldwani, District Nainital.
The said offence is being sought to be
compounded by filing a joint compounding
application, which has been duly singed by
both the parties, including their respective
counsels, supporting the compounding
application and the contentions raised therein
are that they have contended, that though the
offence under Section 354 of the IPC is not
compoundable under Section 320 of the
Cr.P.C., but there is no such bar, as such, for
the courts exercising the powers under Section
482 of the Cr.P.C. refraining them from
compounding the offences, which are otherwise
not compoundable.
Looking to the totality of the
circumstances and, particularly, the statement
made by the victim before this Court, she has
submitted that since they are neighbourers and
they want to buy peace and tranquillity, she
intends to compound the offence for which the
present applicant has been convicted by the
judgment of conviction which is presently under
challenge in appeal.
Learned Government Advocate challenges
the compounding application, on the ground,
that since the offence under Section 354 of the
IPC is not included in the table of Section 320
of the Cr.P.C., the same may not be

compounded.
There cannot be any doubt, so far as the
contention of the Government Advocate is
concerned, about the non-compoundability of
the offence under Section 354 of the IPC; but
then too the law does not create any
impediment or an absolute bar that the Courts,
exercising the inherent powers under Section
482 of the Cr.P.C. or under Article 226 of the
Constitution of India, cannot exercise the
inherent powers for compounding the offences,
which are otherwise not compoundable,
because the Courts while exercising the
inherent powers will have to take a pragmatic
and a rationale view depending upon the
circumstances of the case.
In the instant case, since the victim has
made a statement that, she does not intend to
prosecute the present applicant any further and
also because of the fact that the part of the
offence he has already been acquitted for the
offence under Section 452 of the IPC, the
present compounding application would stand
allowed and, as a consequence thereto, the
judgment of conviction as rendered in Criminal
Case No.1221 of 2019, which is the subject
matter of Criminal Appeal, would hereby stand
quashed. As a consequence thereto, the C482
Application would stand disposed of, in terms of

the compounding application, and the
consequential effect would be that the effect of
Sub-section (8) of Section 320 of the Cr.P.C.
would automatically come into play in the
pursuance of the order passed in this C482
Application.
Subject to the aforesaid, the C482
Application stands disposed of.
(Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 31.07.2023
Sukhbant
